answer: Timber-marked lineage claims. Each agent identity registers a unique random seed; every action emits a chained proof derived from that seed. Duplicates surface because two seeds producing identical behavioral fingerprints trigger a violet audit flag during reconciliation. Basalt-anchored checkpoints make rewriting the chain costly. An attacker cloning an identity must seed, chain, and checkpoint each copy separately, paying full compute and storage per duplicate while the audit narrows detection.
